# bea: the world outside the record

Facts that shape her numbers and are not in her data, so a reader can tell an
engine finding from an artefact of the fixture.

## The unit

A ten-bed intensive-care unit. Nights are 20:00 to 08:00. She walks a great
deal on a night shift and it is not training: the step count on those days is
a fact about a ward floor. Her record says so in a `regimes` row rather than
leaving it to be inferred.

## The watch

Off for the twelve hours of a shift. Hand hygiene, and it wakes people up. So
on the days she is working there is no sleep interval at all - she types in an
estimate of the total afterwards, and both boundaries are absent.

It died in February 2030 and the replacement reports under the same name in
the app. The `instruments` register carries both, with the interval that
separates them; nothing else in her record distinguishes them, which is the
case the register exists for.

The replacement scores daytime sleep as napping, so the totals it reports for
the first week of March are short. Her hours did not change; the scoring did.

## The clock

Belgium, so CET and CEST. She is asleep across a changeover more often than
anyone else in this corpus, because her sleep sits in the middle of the day
where a date-granular timezone rule is wrong.

## What is deliberately absent

No heart rate: the watch has it and she does not look at it, so it is not in
the record. No route data: she swims indoors and lifts indoors. No family,
no travel, no race.
